summary: Implemented per-app and name-allocation locks in src/platform/lock.ts and cross-app declared-port checks in src/registry/ports.ts. Locks record pid and start time, publish atomically, fail immediately with exit 6 naming the holder, reclaim dead-pid or malformed locks, and release on every throw path. Ports reject privileged/out-of-range values with exit 1 and duplicate declarations with exit 6 regardless of bind address. Typecheck, lint, build, the 26 focused tests, and the full 263-test suite pass.

Locks record pid and start time, publish atomically, fail immediately with exit 6 naming the holder, reclaim dead-pid or malformed locks, and release on every throw path. Ports reject privileged/out-of-range values with exit 1 and duplicate declarations with exit 6 regardless of bind address. decisions: App lock file is <appDir>/.lock; the short-lived allocation lock is <appsDir>/.<name>.allocation.lock, a plain file the registry listing ignores.

Lock documents are {schemaVersion, pid, startedAt, operation, app, token} with mode 0600, written to a same-directory temp file and hard-linked into place so another process never observes a partial lock.
A live holder raises ConflictError LOCK_HELD (exit 6) that names the pid, operation, app, and start time; a lock whose pid is dead or whose document is unparseable is reclaimed.
Stale reclamation renames the lock to a unique quarantine path and verifies the bytes are unchanged before deleting, so it cannot remove a lock a third process just acquired.
Release verifies the acquisition token first, so a process never deletes a lock another holder replaced; withAppLock and withAllocationLock release in finally.
Port conflicts compare equality only and never bind addresses; the requesting app's own claim is skipped when options.app is supplied so updates can keep their port.

Missing app directory, unreadable lock file, and unwritable lock location are PrerequisiteError exit 2 (LOCK_DIRECTORY_MISSING, LOCK_UNREADABLE, LOCK_NOT_WRITABLE); contention is exit 6. No new error classes were invented.
interfaces: LockAcquireOptions {app?, operation?, pid?, clock?, isProcessAlive?, maxReclaimAttempts?}
warnings: Stale detection uses pid liveness only; a reused pid could keep an abandoned lock until that unrelated process exits. startedAt is recorded for diagnostics but not compared against /proc start time.
App locks are strictly non-blocking, matching REG-FR-05's immediate exit-6 rule; callers that want to wait must retry themselves.
The allocation lock is created in apps/ as a hidden plain file; Registry.list ignores plain files, so it cannot appear as a broken app.
validationLimitations: The conditional gated host check `EASY_HOST_INTEGRATION=1 npm run test:integration -- tests/integration/add.test.ts` was not run because tests/integration/add.test.ts does not exist yet (ADD phase).
payload.taskDescription: Implement lock.ts with an exclusive lock file inside the app directory that records pid and start time, fails immediately with exit code 6 when held by a live process, and reclaims a lock whose process no longer exists. Implement ports.ts to reject a declared port already used by another app and to reject privileged ports. Tests cover acquire, release, contention, stale reclamation, lock release on error, and port conflicts across apps with different bind addresses.
